study.title: Acupuncture on GB34 activates the precentral gyrus and prefrontal cortex in Parkinson's disease
study.study_design: functional magnetic resonance imaging study comparing brain activation in response to acupuncture in patients with PD and healthy participants; block design
study.population: 12 idiopathic patients with Parkinson's disease and 12 healthy participants matched for age and gender
study.inclusion_criteria: PD participants: diagnosed with clinically definite idiopathic PD by a neurologist from the Kyung Hee Medical Hospital; Hoehn and Yahr stage 1, 2, or 2.5; right-handed (Edinburgh Handedness Inventory); familiar with acupuncture stimulation. Healthy participants: without any neurological or psychiatric history; right-handed; familiar with acupuncture stimulation.
study.exclusion_criteria: Patients with atypical parkinsonian disorder, other neurological or major medical conditions (e.g. head injury, stroke) or current psychiatric problems were excluded from the study.

conditions.timepoint_exact: 5 minutes duration; conducted after structural imaging
conditions.scan_context: fMRI scanning during verum acupuncture stimulation on right GB 34; block design with stimulated and not-stimulated blocks

conditions.timepoint_exact: 5 minutes duration; conducted first before structural imaging
conditions.scan_context: fMRI scanning during sham acupuncture stimulation on right GB 34 using blunt type needle not inserted into skin
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Description explicitly states a blunt needle 'not inserted into skin', indicating surface contact only with no skin penetration. This is a classic Level 3 sham (surface contact, no penetration).

interventions.manipulation_exact: blocks in which the needle was 'stimulated': needle rotated bidirectionally at 1 Hz; blocks in which the needle was 'not stimulated': needle only inserted into the skin and then left in place

extraction_notes.note: Additional file 4: Table S2 contains full neural response coordinates for healthy participants and patients with PD during ACUP and SHAM (one-sample t-test). This supplement was not provided in the PDF. Consequently, individual peak coordinates for the one-sample t-test contrasts (con_HC_ACUP_onesample, con_HC_SHAM_onesample, con_PD_ACUP_onesample, con_PD_SHAM_onesample) cannot be extracted and are reported as narrative_only.

Additional file 1: Table S1 (Demographic characteristics among patients with PD and healthy participants) was not provided in the PDF. Exact age, gender, disease duration, and other demographic details per participant are not fully extractable beyond what is mentioned in the methods text.

Additional file 5: Figure S3 shows comparison of brain activation between PD and healthy participants. The figure was not fully readable from the PDF. Coordinates for this contrast were extracted from Table 2 in the main text.

Table 2 cluster size values (9920 for Healthy > PD; 18776 for PD > Healthy) appear to represent single cluster sizes encompassing multiple peak voxels within the same cluster. The paper does not explicitly state the unit (voxels vs. mm3). The voxel size given is 2.4 × 2.4 × 4.5 mm. Cluster extent unit labeled as 'voxels (inferred)' in extracted rows.

The paper states all local maxima are reported as Talairach coordinates, but the normalization template used was the SPM MNI T1 template. There is a potential discrepancy between MNI normalization and Talairach coordinate reporting. The paper mentions use of Talairach Client software for conversion/labeling, suggesting coordinates were converted from MNI to Talairach. This is not fully clarified in the text.

The one-sample t-test results for healthy participants and PD patients during ACUP and SHAM (Table 1) are presented as a presence/absence summary table with region names only, without coordinates. Coordinates for these contrasts are only available in Additional file 4: Table S2 (supplement not provided).
No adverse events section was present in the paper. The paper does not explicitly state whether adverse events occurred or were monitored.
Expectancy, blinding success, credibility, and allocation guessing were not formally assessed or reported. Only prior acupuncture familiarity is mentioned as a control measure.
Clinical outcome results from the Korean Mini-Mental State Examination and Beck Depression Inventory are mentioned as administered but no numeric results are reported in the main text.
The paper does not clarify whether the 'off' medication condition was verified by plasma levels or purely by time (12 hours after withholding anti-parkinsonian drugs).

Figure 2 reports volume data for precentral gyrus and prefrontal cortex (ACUP vs SHAM paired-t test) but exact numeric volume values are only visible in the figure (bar graphs with error bars) and are not tabulated in the text. The significance level is stated as *P < 0.05.
Figure 3 reports volume of common areas (ACUP vs SHAM) with significance *P < 0.005, but exact numeric volume values are only in the figure and not tabulated in the text.

Table 2 lists Hippocampus under 'Temporal lobe' with Brodmann area column showing no value listed, and coordinates x=32, y=-35, z=0 for the Right hemisphere. The Brodmann area cell appears empty in the table for Hippocampus. Extracted as 'not_reported' for brodmann_area_exact.

The paper describes the scanning experiment starting with SHAM (5 min), then structural imaging (>15 min), then ACUP (5 min). This fixed order may introduce order effects. Whether randomization of condition order occurred is not stated.

Deqi sensations were not separately assessed or reported. The sensation rating instrument used a simple 0-10 intensity scale and was not a validated deqi questionnaire (e.g., MASS, MGH Acupuncture Sensation Scale, or similar).
